newsitem.title: USA: Saudi may not cut oil output if Iraq embargo ends.
newsitem.headline: Saudi may not cut oil output if Iraq embargo ends.

text.p: Saudi Arabia might not need to cut its oil production if the United Nations lifts sanctions against Iraq, a top Saudi oil official said Friday.

"No we'd not necessarily," deputy oil minister Prince Abdel Aziz bin Salman said, responding to a question about whether Saudi Arabia would reduce its output if Iraq was allowed to produce a full three million barrels per day.

Iraq recently resumed limited exports of oil under a U.N. deal allowing it to sell $2 billion worth of oil for food over six months. But sanctions that were imposed in 1990 when Iraq invaded Kuwait remain in force.

"What we live now is in a period in which conditions are better than what it used to be in the past years," Abdel Aziz said in a television broadcast on Middle East Broadcasting Corp., coordinated with the U.S. Information Agency.
"It is expected that the growth in demand would stay within these parameters," he said.
He spoke in Arabic with a simultaneous translation provided by USIA.
"Consequently ... the issue of the return of Iraq again would not impact the production or reduction of (OPEC) member countries," he said.
